propositions: Compaction writes SNAPSHOT.json and *.retired untracked, then commits; if the detached sweep worker dies before commit, the working tree is left dirty with untracked regenerable artifacts and deleted .archived files.

Union-merge in reconverge runs git merge origin/tickets; when origin has committed the same *.retired/SNAPSHOT paths, git aborts with untracked-working-tree-files-would-be-overwritten-by-merge because those paths exist untracked locally.

Push-recovery's abort handler is abort-only and uses git reset --hard (tracked-only) and stash without -u, so it cannot clear untracked files; every retry re-aborts identically, wedging the store and stranding local commits off origin.

The fix detects the untracked-overwrite abort signature, parses the exact paths git names, relocates only those paths to a quarantine directory outside the worktree, then retries the merge once; on retry success both parents are kept and no local commit is orphaned.

The quarantine relocation is safe because only paths git explicitly names are moved (files that already exist on origin), and .tmp-event-* real uncommitted events live at tracker root and do not exist on origin so are never named by git.

Pre-existing tracked .archived deletions left in the worktree by interrupted compaction still fail git status checks in plan-review gates; remediation requires git rm --cached and worker-death cleanup to prevent re-dirtying.
